item.description:
Worktrees, made simple

Wortel 2026.42.1 · 2026-10-15

New Worktree Session (⇧⌘N). A new session in a worktree of its own, on a fresh branch from your default branch, ready at once. Once the session has a name, its branch is named after it too. The files a project needs to run but git ignores, like .env, are copied in; list any others in a .worktreeinclude file.

Open Branch (⇧⌘O). One field for any branch, worktree or pull request. Type a name and Wortel goes to the session already there, continues a closed one, opens the worktree, checks the branch out in a new worktree, or creates it. Each row says which before you press Return, so a branch never gets a second worktree. Type #123 or paste a GitHub or GitLab link to check out a pull request.

Closing keeps your work. Closing a worktree session (⇧⌘W, the ×, or exit) puts it away: the worktree, the branch and the agent’s conversation all stay. Find it with ⇧⌘O and it picks up where it left off. When there’s nothing in it worth keeping, the worktree goes to the Trash instead. Clean Up Worktrees now knows a squash merged branch is merged.

Fork Session (⌥⇧⌘N). The session as it is, in a worktree of its own: staged, unstaged and new files, and the agent’s conversation, forked. Try something without touching the original.

Any worktree, whoever made it. Worktrees you made yourself or with another tool show up in ⇧⌘O and open as sessions, and Wortel never deletes one it didn’t make. A repository can choose where its worktrees go, with Worktree Location… in the folder’s menu or git config wortel.worktreePath.

Ports of their own. Every session gets ten ports to itself, the first in WORTEL_PORT, so two agents running a dev server in two worktrees don’t both want port 3000.

Know why a session stopped. A Claude turn that ended on an API error now says it failed, with the error, and one waiting on a question or a plan says it needs you. Both used to read as finished. While any session is waiting on you, a menu bar item shows how many and lists them.

Also in this release: hold ⌘ to see each session’s ⌘1 to ⌘9 shortcut on its row; closing the last session leaves an empty window instead of quitting; drop a folder on the sidebar or the Dock icon to open it; the shell in a worktree session starts in its worktree, never in /; Claude follows the Mac between light and dark again after Wortel restarts; the git panel names other worktrees after the session in them; very long commands show in the title too; and the pull request button in the git panel is gone, with the network check it made every minute.

Agents come back where they were

Wortel 2026.41.9 · 2026-10-10

The right conversation, every time. After a /clear or /resume inside Claude Code, a session that had to be brought back reopened the conversation Claude was started in, not the one it was in. Wortel now keeps track of the conversation while the agent runs.

Nothing left behind. When the process that keeps your terminals running was stopped, an agent that happened to finish closing first was taken as one you had quit, and stayed closed. Each terminal now comes back when its own shell ends, and a resume counts as done only once the agent is running again.

Started the way you started it. A resumed agent keeps --dangerously-skip-permissions, its model, its permission mode, an environment variable in front of it, and a wrapper like devx pi. Before, it came back asking for permission at every step. A command line with more than one command in it is typed for you rather than run again.

Agents found in more places. Aliases, npx and bunx, cd project && claude, and an agent you suspend with Ctrl-Z and bring back with fg are all followed now. ssh host claude and tmux new claude are no longer mistaken for an agent running in Wortel.

Typing exit ends the session. A shell that ended used to leave a terminal that did nothing.

Also in this release: a full restore no longer holds the window up for half a second per session; the process that keeps your terminals is replaced once it holds none when it came from an older version, which is what kept Full Disk Access from reaching your shells after an update; a missed reply can no longer hand one session’s terminal to another; and prompts are faster in zsh and bash.

Colours, and a Fork that shows its work

Wortel 2026.41.8 · 2026-10-09

Colour a session. Right-click a session, or open its ”…” menu, and pick a colour: a bar at the edge of its row marks it, say yellow for a review waiting on CI. Only you take it off. From a terminal, wortel mark yellow does the same, and wortel mark none clears it.

Fork shows its work. The new session appears the moment you press Create, and its page says the worktree is being prepared while you keep working in your other sessions. Its terminal opens when it’s ready. If git refuses, the page says why, with Try Again. Forking a repository that uses Git LFS works now too: Wortel couldn’t find git-lfs when it was installed with Homebrew or Nix.

Permissions. Wortel ▸ Permissions… shows whether notifications are on and whether Wortel has Full Disk Access, with a button to change each. While notifications are off, a hand with an orange dot in the sidebar says so.

Camera, microphone and the rest. A program you run in Wortel that needs the camera, the microphone, your contacts or another app now gets the usual macOS prompt. Before, macOS turned it down without asking.

Clean Up Worktrees, faster. The list appears at once with each branch’s name, checks several worktrees at the same time, and each row says what it’s doing.

Also in this release: a worktree session always shows its branch under its name, never the folder you happen to be in. And dragging a session shows the whole row.
